full_judgment:
2. Plaintiff Abdul Awal on the following averments filed the suit for pre-emption under Mohammadan Law. It is his case that Bashirullah was the owner of the suit land of CS khatian No. 19 and SA khatian No.17, died leaving 3 sons, Siddique Ahmed, Sultan Ahmed and Khaiz Ahmed and 3 daughters, Firoza Khatun, Mamuna Khatun, Maksuda Khatun by his first wife and 2 daughters, Golnahar and Fatema Khatun by his 2 wife and 2nd wife Amena Khatun. Out of the heirs, Siddique Ahmed died leaving plaintiff, defendant Nos.5 and 6 as three sons, one daughter, defendant No.7 and wife, defendant No-8. Other heirs of Bashirullah also died leaving heirs as well. Plaintiff is a co-sharer by inheritance in the suit land. Plaintiff used to live in Dhaka. Plaintiff came to the village on 15-3-2002 and learned to know that the suit land has been transferred. Immediately plaintiff has performed the formalities of Talab-I-Ishad and Talab-i-Mowasibat in presence of witnesses and tendered price money to defendant No. l. But defendant No.1 did not pay any heed to this issue as such, plaintiff after obtaining certified copy on 17-4-2002 definitely came to know about the sale that defendant Nos.2-4 sold the suit land to defendant No.1 by Ewaz deed No.517 dated 28-1-1999. Plaintiff case is that exchange deed was made to overcome the right of pre-emption, filed the suit. 

 3. Petitioner as defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint and after taking all the preliminary objections as to maintainability of the suit, it is her case that Basirullah sold 44 decimals of land by deed No.4330 dated 23-9-1946 to the predecessor of defendant No. 1. Rustam Mia, Sultan Ahmed, son of Basirullah, sold to Rustam Mian 33 decimals of land by deed No.6227 dated 1-12-1957. SA khatian No. 17 rightly recorded his name along with others, as such, he was a co-sharer in the suit land. Rustom Mian died leaving Makbul Ahmed and 8 sons, one daughter, Hajera Begum. Makbul Ahmed died leaving 4 sons including defendant Nos. l and 4. The heirs of Basirullah were also co-sharer in the suit jote. Khaiz Ahmed, son of Basirullah died leaving wife, Halima Begum and Rokeya Begum and others as 3 daughters, Jamaluddin and others as 3 sons. In this way defendant Nos.2-4 became owners in the suit jote and they have transferred the suit plot to defendant No.1 by ewaj deed No.517 dated 28-1-1999. Defendant No.1 become the owner in that land and possessing the land to the knowledge of the plaintiff since transfer. Plaintiff is not entitled to claim pre-emption as he is no way co-sharer in the suit jote. Moreover, defendant No. 17 added after he has filed Miscellaneous Case No.62 of 2007. She has obtained a compromise decree in terms of solenama against the ewaj deed in question hence the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 11. Mr Rafiqul Islam Sohel, learned Advocate, appearing for the defendant-petitioner, submits that, Courts below concurrently failed to consider that defendant No.1 is a co-sharer by inheritance as such if any transfer made in favour of defendant No.1 then it is hit by provision of law. Learned Advocate referred to the case of Abdul Haque Miah vs Abdur Rashid, 1983 BLD (AD) 103 = 35 DLR (AD) 54. Learned Advocate next submits that transfer was made on 28-1-1999, suit has been filed on 9-6-2002, the suit having been filed long after period of limitation, is barred by limitation under Mohammadan Law, Mohammadan Law prescribed filing of suit within one year from the date of transfer. Learned Advocate further submits that pre-emptor-plaintiff having not been co-sharer, he has no locus standi to file the suit. Learned Advocate further submits that after purchase, khatian has been split up and jama has been separated, as such, suit for pre-emption ought not to be decreed.
